committed_turns.public_event: A newcomer has reached the card room.
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: A coin rings off the table edge and wobbles across the floor toward the south door, and nobody at the card table moves to catch it. Four of them sit at a worn table near that door, pale as candle tallow, pointed teeth showing when they breathe, dressed in lace and velvet gone shiny at the elbows. Each has coins stacked in front of them; a silver ring sits among the stacks in the middle. The man dealing has stopped mid-hand, one card pinned between two fingers. Beyond them, the whole north wall is a carved mountain, tiny dwarves in tiny caverns, stone sunbeams fanning over a long tub sunk into the floor.
Narrator: When the dealer speaks it is slow and savoring, each word laid down like a card he means you to look at.
Dealer: Well, now. The door brought us company. Come in, come in, the passage is draftier than we are. That coin by your boot is the most interesting thing that has happened at this table in an hour, so tell me: are you the sort who picks it up, or the sort who waits to see whose it is?

committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "Whatever you're selling, I'm not buying. I'm just passing through."
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: The card stops turning. The drawl goes out of him like a lamp being trimmed.
Dealer: Passing through. Everyone is passing through, friend. That is the whole business. Ten gold. That is what passing costs, paid to me, here, before you touch that door. Pay it and nobody at this table remembers your face. That's the offer. It is the only thing I am selling tonight, so you are going to have to buy it or tell me why not.
Narrator: The player nearest the door scrapes his chair around until it faces the door instead of the table, and picks his cards back up as if nothing happened.

appraisal.cause: The newcomer shuts the conversation down and states an intent to pass straight through.
appraisal.label: interest

improv_read.connection: The gang extorts newcomers here; someone who announces they are passing through has just asked for the one thing the dealer sells, so he names the price now, crisply.
improv_read.kit_choice: A flat brush-off meets the room as it really is: a toll station. Kit lets the price land without softening it and without comment.
improv_read.player_bid: Refuses whatever the dealer is offering and says they are only passing through.

committed_turns.player_input: Ten gold to cross a room? No. Not a copper. Move your chair.
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "Ten gold to cross a room? No. Not a copper. Move your chair."
committed_turns.spoken:
Kit: No roll. Nobody has moved yet; a no is just a no until someone makes it more.
Dealer: Not a copper. Then you are either rich enough not to care or poor enough to be dangerous, and I cannot tell which from here. So let us count together. Four of us. One of you. And a chair, which my friend is very fond of, between you and that door. Tell me what you think happens when you walk past it.
Narrator: The player by the fresco lays his cards face down, very neatly, and flexes his fingers one at a time. The one by the door does not move his chair.

appraisal.cause: A second flat refusal, now with an order to the man by the door; the stakes just rose on the player’s own initiative.
appraisal.label: interest

improv_read.connection: He wants control without risking himself; open violence is a risk, so he turns the refusal into a public test of nerve and makes the newcomer imagine the fight instead of starting one.
improv_read.kit_choice: The player escalated; Kit states the ruling position exactly so the refusal carries its real weight, then lets the dealer answer it.
improv_read.player_bid: Refuses the ten gold outright and orders the man by the door to move his chair.

trace.observed_event: You declare: "Ten gold to cross a room? No. Not a copper. Move your chair."

public_brief.kit_focus: Say plainly that a refusal starts no fight and needs no roll, then let the table carry the menace in stillness.
public_brief.objective: Regain control of the room without being the one who starts a fight.
public_brief.player_opening: The newcomer can walk, back down, bargain, or escalate further.
public_brief.reply_to: Not a copper. Move your chair.
public_brief.tactic: Answer the refusal by weighing the newcomer aloud, then lay out the odds and ask them to picture walking past his chair.
public_brief.visible_cue: The player by the fresco sets down his cards and flexes his hands; the dealer does not stand.

committed_turns.player_input: I walk to the south door without another word.
committed_turns.public_event: You go through the south door into the short passage.
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: You go through the south door into the short passage.
Narrator: Nobody stands. The chair by the door stays exactly where it is, and you pass close enough to it to smell candle wax and cheap rosewater. The dealer lets you get your hand on the door before he speaks, loud enough for his table.
Dealer: Let them go, let them go. Call it a gift from the house. Friend, the ones further down do not play cards and they do not take no twice. When they ask you for more than ten gold, and they will, remember whose offer you walked out on. You can always come back and apologize.
Narrator: The door closes on laughter that goes on a little too long.

appraisal.cause: The newcomer walks out past a toll the gang openly demanded; the room lets it happen.
appraisal.label: concern

improv_read.connection: The dealer could not extort this newcomer and will not risk himself stopping them; the source says the gang then prefers to point such people at other trouble deeper in.
improv_read.kit_choice: Kit does not reward or punish the walk-out; she lets the dealer save face in public and plant a threat about what lies further in, without inventing anything specific.
improv_read.player_bid: Walks to the south door and leaves without answering.

trace.observed_event: You go through the south door into the short passage.

public_brief.objective: Save face in front of his table and make the newcomer someone else’s problem.
public_brief.player_opening: The newcomer is in the passage; they can keep going, turn back, or answer.
public_brief.reply_to: I walk to the south door
public_brief.tactic: Call after the newcomer, pretending the passage was his gift, and warn that others further in will not be as polite.
public_brief.visible_cue: Behind the closing door, laughter from the table that sounds forced.
